steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Woooah, this dress looks absolutely stunning!

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: You'n say that again. Sora's gonna look mighty fine in it.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: If someone told me about this earlier, I would've signed up myself!

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: No way, no how. Ya don't know the first thing about actin'.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I can just act like I always do.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: And there ain't no roles for a Sankta in Siracusa neither!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Says who? I heard that there was a Sankta with Signora Sicilia—

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Frivolous Mafioso
steps.text: Signorina Sally, our boss is inviting you over for dinner.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Um... But...

steps.name: Stony-Faced Bodyguard
steps.text: She's on her way to rehearsal right now. Vaffanculo.

steps.name: Frivolous Mafioso
steps.text: And our boss wants to have a word with Signorina Sally here. Being a little late won't make a difference, will it?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: I, I'll go get the director...

steps.name: Frivolous Mafioso
steps.text: The director? I might've carried water for him in the past, but these days...

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Um, please don't...

steps.name: Angry Mafioso
steps.text: The hell are you playin' nice with them for?

steps.name: Angry Mafioso
steps.text: You should feel honored that our boss wants to see you. If you don't wanna get messed up, behave yourself and come with us.

steps.name: Frivolous Mafioso
steps.text: Wait, the boss didn't say we could—

steps.name: Angry Mafioso
steps.text: You still don't understand what the boss was gettin' at? We were all scared of the Bellones before.

steps.name: Angry Mafioso
steps.text: But now that they are out of the picture, and the bigwigs are about to shuffle the deck again, we'll never get a better chance!

steps.name: Frivolous Mafioso
steps.text: Huh, you're right. Let's go, brothers, time to clean the streets of these eyesores!

steps.name: Stony-Faced Bodyguard
steps.text: Tch... Protect Signorina Sally!

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: The heck's happenin', Exu— Huh? Where'd she go?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: She already rushed out. Let's back her up!

steps.name: Stony-Faced Bodyguard
steps.text: Urgh...

steps.name: Frivolous Mafioso
steps.text: Heh, and you call yourself a bodyguard?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Ahh... *sobs*...

steps.name: Frivolous Mafioso
steps.text: Right this way, signorina.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: I, I know...

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Huh? You people are—

steps.name: Frivolous Mafioso
steps.text: Who the hell are you?!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Catch me if you can.

steps.name: Frivolous Mafioso
steps.text: Tch, get her!

steps.name: Angry Mafioso
steps.text: Don't mess with us!

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Let's split!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Your name's Sally, right? You okay?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Do you know what you've done?!

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: You didn't save me at all, you're just making things worse! They're not going to let this go!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: So how'd you plan to get out of that mess?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: ...By gritting my teeth.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Huh? But they were gonna hurt you.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: I... can deal with injuries.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Did you really think they were going to kidnap me? They're just trying to cause trouble.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Shouldn't you at least call for help when stuff like this happens?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: What's the point? Nobody's going to intervene in a struggle between famiglie.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What about that Judge Lavinia lady? She seemed like a pretty decent person to me.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: She's... indeed a very good judge, but there's nothing she can do in these situations.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Besides, even if I never made it out of this park, how many people would know that I disappeared because of the conflict between those mafiosi?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: So... you're just going to put up with it?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: How else are we supposed to live our lives? This is how it's always been.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Find a place to hide, wait until the dust settles, and then follow the victorious side out. That's all I can do.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: But... why does it have to be like that?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Ugh, I'm sorry. I'm not trying to blame you, but to be honest, this is the first time in my life I've ever known what it feels like to be protected.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: That famiglia isn't even particularly influential. The director should be able to help me smooth things over.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: But just as a friendly word of advice, if you plan to stay alive in Siracusa, please try to avoid doing that kind of stuff in the future.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Especially considering what's about to happen.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What's about to happen?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Have you not seen the news at all? Carracci, Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici, is dead.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Yeah, saw that. Assassinated, looks like?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: I feel so bad for him.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Since you all seem nice enough, I'll tell you a little more about him.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: I have to deal with mafiosi pretty regularly, so I've heard a thing or two from them.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: The person who murdered him hasn't been found yet, and the young master of Famiglia Bellone was also attacked at the same time.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Huh? Bellone?!

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: That's right. The Bellones were poised to stand head and shoulders above the other famiglie, but it seems like someone's been plotting against them for a while now.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Many famiglie that had previously given up are now starting to move again, little by little.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Did you hear any of them mention the name Texas?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Texas? There's not a single person in Siracusa who doesn't know that name.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: But usually in the context of 'the last Texas' or something along those lines...

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Really?!

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: You're a strange one, you know that? It's obviously all made-up. How could there possibly be a Texas still alive out there?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: But... Alright, you have a point.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: In any case, you should already know that our troupe has some connections to Famiglia Bellone, through the director.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Just as those people were saying, in the past everyone wanted to get on his good side. But now...

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: You all saw what happened.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Do all of Siracusa's famiglie go around doing whatever the hell they want like that?

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: ...Remember what I'm about to tell you.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: If you want to survive in Siracusa, you either need to join a famiglia, or stay as far away from them as possible.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Then... you need to delude yourself into believing that as long as you stay away from them, you won't get sucked into any trouble.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Alright, I should head back to the theater now.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Aaaaaaaahhhh—!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What now?!

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: S-Someone's been tied up over here!

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Assuming nothin' outta the ordinary happened, someone ought to have found the poor fella by now.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: I don't get it, man. Why go through all that trouble keeping him alive, just to let him go? What's so special about that guy anyway?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: What it proves is, that shady bartender wanted him to be found.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: As for why... it's usually a trap.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Tch, what a sinister fella.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: You say that now, but if he ends up winning, you're gonna be calling him a genius.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Dipshit.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: What's so funny?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: I just remembered how we used to argue like this back when we were kids.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Never would've imagined that after all these years, after all of life's twists and turns, the two of us'd still be out here, fightin' for our lives.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: That's fate for you. Never know where it's gonna take you.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Heh. Ain't that the truth.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Who could've known something like that would happen in Lungmen?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: And that after all that, we'd still come back to Siracusa.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Gambino... If, and I mean if, Lappland has really decided to leave us alone, and let us fend for ourselves...

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Would you still stay in Siracusa?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: What, do you miss your Lungmen that bad?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Hmph. Forget it, not like you'd ever understand anyway.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Let's talk about something more practical. You really plan on switching employers?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Looking at the news, the guy we tried to off today was Don Bellone's son. Seems like someone real important died at the same time.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Which sounds to me an awful lot like some unknown famiglia has been using us as their weapons.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Might as well go make that relationship formal, then.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Better than taking on odd jobs and begging for scraps.
That's right. As soon as you're back in Siracusa, you participate in an attempted assassination of one of the Dodici dons. You two sure have grown.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Guess the good ol' days are over...

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Lappland...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh? Today's breakfast is looking pretty good.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Pay for your own.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Aw, is that any way to treat your boss?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: So, what've you been up to all this time?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I went to say hi to the folks, and got to enjoy some sorely-missed family time. Simple as that.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Haah, what a relief that despicable old mug back home is just as punchable as it's always been.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: You with a famiglia?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh, did I never mention it? My last name is Saluzzo.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Saluzzo?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: You're a Saluzzo?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Capone, do you know what the thing I hate the third most is?
Capone feels a chill course through his body, but the sensation is so fleeting that he has to wonder if it was his imagination.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: When people start wailing and moaning once they hear the name of my famiglia.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Ah, come to think of it, the way you do things really does remind me of that one famiglia.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: What about the other two things? If I'm gonna die, might as well die knowing.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Haha. Seems like you've picked up on how to get along with me.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Actually, I just came up with that line on the spot.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Tch.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Alright, talk to me. So why'd the two of you decide to do a hit on Famiglia Bellone?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Sorry for bothering you, Signor Segretario.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: No, no, Your Honor, the pleasure is mine.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Your office is... quite impressive.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Haha, I frequently have distinguished guests here, and this is the sort of decor they prefer, so I figured I'd go along with it.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: So, did you need me for something?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I wanted to talk to you about Carracci's death.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Hmm? I believe I already made a statement about that.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But I wanted to have a chat with you, for more personal reasons.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Oh right... I heard you swore you'd find Carracci's murderer and bring them to justice.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Good, good. Young folks ought to have that kind of drive.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: So have you made any progress?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Unfortunately, not yet.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Sorry to hear that.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I heard you'd always been on good terms with him personally, so...

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: That's true. Carracci was greatly concerned with the citizenry's well being, things such as food, water, and sanitation.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: But I don't think there's anything I can do to assist you.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: I never actually mingled my way into his innermost circle.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: So while I'd love to help, there's nothing I can do.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Anything you can give me is fine. A place you think is suspicious, or anyone in the government I should keep an eye on.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: You're asking too much. You understand what I'm saying, don't you?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Your Honor... several other Ministri dei Lavori Pubblici died before Carracci. Do you remember them?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Seven? Or maybe eight?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: The people in those positions were just puppets. Each famiglia was trying to push their own people up there.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: But in the end, they were all taken out by other famiglie.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: When it came to a position as important as il Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici, though, I'll be blunt here, it was clear as day why the famiglie filled the position with a man as spotless as Carracci instead of installing one of their cronies.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: For one simple reason: if the killing continued, the construction of the city would grind to a halt.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: 'If our people can't get in, then we'll at least make sure yours can't either.' That is why Carracci occupied that seat.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Make no mistake, he had close ties with the Bellones. The Don's son even sat beside him as his secretary. But, in one way or another, he was just as close with every other famiglia.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: There's an ancient Yan saying to the effect of 'he who walks oft along the river, inevitably finds his shoes wet,' yes? I have always trusted in Carracci's integrity, but so what? Others did not see it that way.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: The way Siracusans think, you either choose to be one famiglia's pet, or you choose to be another's.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: In other words, Carracci's death was inevitable. He wasn't part of any of famiglia's vision for the future. Do you think he was oblivious to that fact?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: In the end, it doesn't matter whether he died today, a month ago, or a month from now.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You know how much hard work he put in.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: And what did he get for it in the end?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Actually, let's assume he was as selfless a person as you say. What did the people he worked so hard for, those whom he so eloquently claimed as 'his dear citizens,' give him in the end?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Your Honor, I've also heard a great many rumors about you.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: You undeniably have a fair number of accomplishments under your belt.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: But among them, how many were due solely to your own hard work, and how many were influenced by the people behind your back? You already know the answer, don't you?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: If I may be frank, Your Honor, are you really not here to test me on behalf of Bellone?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That is not my intention, I swear.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: ...I'd prefer it were.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Then please heed this word of caution, Your Honor.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Let those who've died stay dead.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: We already have too much to worry about without overly concerning ourselves with the deceased.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: And... this is the attitude of someone who was on good terms with him?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: If you want to have a slightly longer lease on life in Volsinii's government, I'd suggest you learn this lesson well.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Oh, hello sweetheart. Ah, I'm still at work right now. Are you ready to go?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Mm, alright. I'll get ready to head over then.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Okay, okay.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: That was my daughter. Now, a newly-opened restaurant has invited me to inspect their ingredients tonight.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: We'll have to set aside our discussion for later.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Oh right, please let Master Leontuzzo know that he is welcome to talk to me if he's interested in the gourmet experience.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...I'll remember to pass it on.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Now then, please see yourself out.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: What did you say? You found someone unconscious and tied up? The leader of the bunch that attacked the restaurant?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Understood. I'll be there right away.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: I'm telling you, the two of us just happened to be involved in that hit. We don't know nothing.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: As for the guy who handed out the orders, we don't know which famiglia he belongs to, but he sure was generous with the cash.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: They were clearly looking for hitmen with murky backgrounds like you two, so when you die, there'd be no trail back to who hired you.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You might think you ran into them by chance, but it wouldn't surprise me if they had their eyes on you a long time ago.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: I'm not saying they didn't.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: So, want to take a crack at who your employer is?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Probably... the Rossatis or the Saluzzos. Of the Dodici who've been fighting over this city all this time, and with the Bellones out of the picture, they're the only two famiglie with enough power left.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Right, I'm sure most people would think the same.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But now you know the Saluzzos were never planning anything like that.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: That just leaves... the Rossatis?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: One more.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Remember those poor suckers you took out early on? They were originally targeting people from il Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Don Bellone's son's been working there, so another way of putting this is that the folks you dealt with were trying to get in Bellone's way.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: So... what you're saying is, we helped the Bellones put down a threat, but then turned right around and hit 'em even harder.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: ...So what? We see famiglie doing that kinda power jockeying stuff every day.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: That... He's got a point. The first hit we made might've just been on some unlucky, short-sighted bastards.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But don't forget, you were specifically sent to 'shut them up.'

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Wait, are you serious?!

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Are you suggesting... there's a double agent inside the Bellones?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Just another possibility.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hahaha, but hey, that's what makes things interesting.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Let's assume that's true and do a little thought experiment here.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Carracci, il Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici, is dead. And before that, several more people in the ministero were killed.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Naturally, most people are going to see those things as connected, especially that poor judge.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But. The perpetrator who carried out the hit has already been silenced, and she can't find their leader either. She's at a complete loss, so what does she do next?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: If only some kind of clue would appear.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: And what do you know, isn't that assassin you dumped out there the best possible lead?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: So that's why they waited until now to throw that guy out...

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: It does make sense, when you put it that way.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Then, they set up a little ambush, and make sure the judge has an 'accident'...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Kaboom.
Lappland stretches out her hands and falls back onto the sofa, as if knocked back by the blast.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Everyone's gonna get pulled in.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Ahh, what a great idea.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It's so great that even if this is all bullshit, I'd want to make it reality.

spans.text: It's so great that even if this is all bullshit, I'd

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: So... lemme get this straight, you two are sayin' that the Bellones are puttin' on a whole goddamn opera?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: It's definitely possible.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: After all, nobody understands the Bellones better than themselves.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Hmph. I don't buy it.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: These are the famiglia's plans for the future we're talking about. There ain't a single wise guy in all of Siracusa who'd attack his own famiglia at a time like this.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Gambino, you should've realized by now that kinda blind confidence is what brought down the Sicilians.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: But I gotta say, I think I agree with you this time.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Aha! Then maybe they're putting on this show to feign weakness, so everyone thinks they're vulnerable and—

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: But they were already on the cusp of victory.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Do you seriously think that the Bellones just decided to give up on a city that was right at their fingertips, just to turn this whole place upside-down?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Are they crazy or something?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Who knows? There are more lunatics walking this land than you might think.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Haha, but I guess our merry mealtime needs to wrap up.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I hope you have a jolly ol' time out there.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: You stopped by just to say hello?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: What, are you that eager to be my henchmen?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: I wouldn't say it's high on my priorities.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: But at least tell us which side you're on.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Last thing I want is to end up fighting against you without realizing, and dying without knowing what hit me.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Me? Naturally, I'll always be Texas's most loyal supporter.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Is everyone in position for the ambush?

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You seem like you want to say something.

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: I was just thinking... I feel bad for Signorina Lavinia.

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: Whatever the case may be, she's a friend to the famiglia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: If only the one she befriended wasn't Leon, the next don of Famiglia Bellone—

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Look, I don't want to be the villain either.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: So she wants to play her little game of justice. Sure, that we can allow, to an extent.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But she thinks she has the backing of one of the bosses. What she's done over the years has had a larger and larger impact on Leon... No, on our entire famiglia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: The Bellones don't need softness like that.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: She must be made crystal-clear of this fact, and so must Leon.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Otherwise...

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We'll never be able to seize ultimate victory from the chaos that's about to ensue.

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: But, the young master, he—

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I know many of you are still conflicted about this. I will assume full responsibility for whatever happens. When Leon eventually comes asking who to blame, I won't get any of you involved.

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

a.text: Cellinia, I need to send you to stay in Siracusa for a while.

The Columbian famiglie changed into opulent attire, took up residence in luxurious mansions, and stepped into the so-called upper class, thinking they had clearly delineated a boundary between them and Siracusa.
'Siracusa is barbaric, while we are not.' They spoke those words, thinking themselves superior to our homeland.
Your father's been captured by this line of thinking too.
As for you, I need you to see for yourself.
See the place we came from. See if we're any different from them.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: ...Who's there?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I've brought you some chocolate. Want some?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I see prison security in Siracusa is as shoddy as ever.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You know, they call this one impregnable, at least compared to other cities.
Texas lets out a tiny sigh, and takes a bite out of the chocolate in Lappland's hand.
It's her least favorite flavor.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hah. And here I thought you'd be chasing me out instead.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: That takes a lot more effort than just ignoring you.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: So long as you don't get in my way, do whatever you want.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Aw, I'm almost moved to tears here, Texas. Even you're gradually figuring out how to get along with me.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I never get in other peoples' way. I'd much rather clear the fog for them, so they can better see where they're going.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: How much do the Saluzzos know?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: No more than you do.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: The Bellones were pretty much a shoo-in to win, but to keep the Rossatis down, they even brought you back from Lungmen, as a precautionary measure of sorts.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But right at the critical moment, yesterday's assassination took place.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It's so blatant that people can't help but think it had to be intentional. Is the perpetrator even trying to stay hidden?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: So what about you? Planning to sit in this cell reminiscing about every little thing that happened in Lungmen until that judge lets you go?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Weren't you in a hurry to get back there?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: If you consider the wait as just another leg of the journey home, then I can be pretty patient.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But what if that judge is in danger?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Where is he? Has he woken up yet?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Good to see you here, Your Honor! We've already taken full control of the scene.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: The suspect is still unconscious, but he was tied up and stuffed into a trash can over by the corner. We've already notified the hospital.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Who found him?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: A group of actors from Compagnia dell'alba. They already left because they had a rehearsal to get to.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Compagnia dell'alba... Bernardo's people?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: He really is cursed with bad luck.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Your Honor, the people murdered in the witness elimination case you reported last time were this person's accomplices, right?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Yes, but we couldn't find anything on them to identify them with.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Why would their leader show up here in such a sorry state then...?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Want me to try waking him up?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Please do.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... *cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Stop struggling. We already have you restrained.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: ...Lavinia.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Do you understand the situation you're in? Who tied you up and dumped you here?

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Do you really need to ask, judge?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Answer my question, murderer.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Heh. Maybe I can invoke Article 14 of the penal code to remain silent under informal investigations.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...You're pretty familiar with the law.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: What, are you gonna use Article 132, the right of special dispensation, on me? Judge?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Just who are you?

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Your average everyday murderer.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I, I remember now... I've seen you before.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Last night at the restaurant, no? You rescued that hapless clerk from il Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: It was three years ago, at a legal forum. Judge Bortolotti from the city of Sorrento gave a particularly outstanding speech.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Signor, I was deeply impressed by your report.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Well, I just kill people for a living now. It's an easy life. What you're talking about, I can barely even remember anymore.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: This isn't who you are.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Stop acting so self-righteous, Lavinia. You really think you understand me? Just from a fantasy-filled report at a window-dressing legal forum?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You can't hide true passion. That's what you said back then.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Right, along with all the other naive, idealistic nonsense I rattled off. All young people are like that, thinking they can change the world all on their own.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: I just happened to wake up sooner than you, Lavinia.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You said, 'we should all strive to find the common line that can protect anyone.'

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Yes, here's an example: join a famiglia, listen to the boss, and kill anyone who gets in your way.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Judge Bortolotti, I can help you.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Hah! Help me?!

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Oh, that's right. You have the great and powerful Bellones backing you.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: Your honor and dignity will stay untarnished. You won't get chained down or beaten up for a moment of naivete. You won't come home to the sight of your house going up in smoke along with your family.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: You don't know a damn thing, Judge Lavinia.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: You have no idea how weighty the code you hold in your hand is, and how easily it can destroy your life.

steps.name: Calm Hitman
steps.text: And luckily for you, you'll never have a chance to find out.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Watch out, Lavinia!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: We need to get out of here, now.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Texas?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: They've sent a ton of people. Come with me.
